problem: Prior IVLN methods (TourHAMT, MAP-CMA) fail to exploit tour memory: naively stacking previous-episode history does not help, while MAP-CMA relies on a closed-set segmenter (13 categories) plus depth and only works in continuous environments. The tour history has no explicit cross-modal supervision.
motivation: IVLN keeps memory across episodes, but this memory is unstructured and only weakly supervised (instruction-path correspondence is coarse and paths can be wrong). A structured, open-vocabulary, setting-agnostic memory could let agents use past observations and generalize to new scenes without annotation or retraining.
key_idea: Use an LLM to extract keywords from instructions and an open-vocabulary detector (OWL-ViT) to ground them in panoramas, storing them in a viewpoint graph (Omnigraph) that is fused locally into the agent's input for both discrete and continuous VLN.
insight: Structured, positional memory of open-vocabulary keywords is what makes tour history useful, whereas raw history stacking does not help. Ablating the view index and distance (Table 4) lowers t-nDTW (val-unseen 54.9 to 50.6 with both removed), and view index matters more. Restricting keywords to 12 categories (Type-I) gives little gain, and open-vocabulary keywords add about 2 points t-nDTW, while an oracle memory (Type-III) is best.
method: Keyword extraction: GPT-3.5 with a system prompt returns milestone noun phrases (with attributes) from each episode's instruction.

Keyword-panoramic detection: OWL-ViT (ViT-L/14) detects the keywords in the panorama at each viewpoint, storing box, label, confidence and absolute heading; viewpoints are revisited and re-detected with new instructions' keywords.
Omnigraph: a graph whose nodes are visited viewpoints tagged with keywords and whose edges are connectivity, incrementally updated across episodes in a tour.

Omnigraph fusion (discrete, HAMT): collects neighbours within d_n=3 steps, keeps the top-confidence box per keyword, assigns discrete distance and view index, and resolves conflicts by the most frequent value. Keyword [CLS] embeddings from the BERT instruction encoder are fused with view-index sin/cos and distance embeddings, sorted by distance, and appended to the text embeddings.

Omnigraph fusion (continuous, MAP-CMA): registers a new viewpoint when >d_vp=1 from all stored ones and runs detection within d_det=0.25. Neighbours within d_n=7 are used, keywords get continuous heading/distance embeddings via linear layers, and instruction-query attention over the keywords feeds the second GRU state encoder.
Unified framework: the same omnigraph plugs into HAMT (IR2R) and MAP-CMA (IR2R-CE) with all original hyperparameters retained; it is also applied to Iterative REVERIE.

setting.backbone: HAMT (discrete) / MAP-CMA (continuous) agents trained with OWL-ViT ViT-L/14 (detector) and GPT-3.5 (keywords)
setting.training_data: IR2R train (14025 episodes, 61 scenes, 3 tours each) and IR2R-CE; Iterative REVERIE tours built with LKH; detector and LLM used off the shelf
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (discrete); RGB-D with semantic/occupancy maps plus panoramic detection (continuous)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (IR2R); low-level continuous actions (IR2R-CE)
setting.privileged: Oracle goal/start teleoperation between episodes in the IVLN protocol; the Type-III ablation uses oracle keyword memory, but the main results do not

numbers.extra: mean of 3 runs; t-nDTW is the tour metric
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (comparison with HAMT and TourHAMT), row 6 Ours, Val-Unseen

numbers.extra: inferred semantics and iterative map construction; mean of 3 runs

numbers_note: All numbers are means over 3 runs (± std omitted). The IR2R, IR2R-CE and Iterative REVERIE benchmarks are not in the canonical list, so they are labelled other:. The Type-III oracle variant (val-unseen t-nDTW 56) is not listed as a main result.
results: On IR2R, OVER-NAV improves t-nDTW over HAMT from 58 to 62 (val-seen) and from 50 to 55 (val-unseen), while TourHAMT is worse than HAMT (t-nDTW 32-45). On IR2R-CE it beats MAP-CMA by 4 and 3 t-nDTW points (56 vs 52 and 50 vs 47). It also improves over HAMT on Iterative REVERIE.
limitations: Requires panoramic observations and an external LLM and OVD detector at every viewpoint, which is computationally costly (a second GPU is needed for detection).

Gains in continuous environments are modest (SR equal to MAP-CMA on val-unseen at 35), and the memory relies on detection quality and on keywords from past instructions only, so it lags the oracle-memory Type-III.
Evaluated only on iterative R2R/R2R-CE plus a brief REVERIE study, with a fixed hand-tuned neighbourhood radius.
